# Phase 5 — baselines B1-B5 versus M5

*Generated by `hydrocascade experiments` on 2026-09-24.*

> ### ⚠ Fitted on synthetic data
>
> `data_mode` is `synthetic` for `glofas`, `landslides`, and 9,764 of 9,765
> catalog rows are synthetic stand-ins. **Every parameter, every lead time and every
> p-value below describes the stand-in generators, not Kerala.** They exist to show
> the experimental machinery runs and that its diagnostics fire. Switching
> `data_mode` to `real` and rerunning turns all of them into results with no code change.


Doc 08 §2: **B5 versus M5 is the single most important comparison in the paper.** It isolates exactly the contribution we claim — the network formulation — because B5 has cross terms but no network, no travel time and no dilution.

| ID | model | established in | what beating it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | climatology (monthly mean rate) | Phase 3 | the floor |
| B2 | rainfall intensity-duration threshold | Phase 3 | **beating current operational practice** |
| B3 | XGBoost susceptibility x rainfall | Phase 3 | beating the strongest ML competitor |
| B4 | two independent single-type Hawkes | Phase 4 code (= A1) | the value of cross-hazard coupling |
| B5 | multitype Hawkes, isotropic Euclidean kernel | Phase 4 code (= A2) | **the value of the network formulation** |
| M5 | full model | Phase 4 | — |

B1-B3 are in `reports/phase3_baselines.md`, measured on the same splits. B4 and B5 are ablations A1 and A2 respectively — the same fits, named for what they isolate rather than for what they remove.

- **B4 (A1)** held-out logL -66,271.31 against M5's -66,083.31 — M5 wins by 187.99.
- **B5 (A2)** held-out logL -65,364.59 against M5's -66,083.31 — M5 does NOT win by 718.72.
